main_text.p: & pluribus utuntur verbis, ut vim hujus verbi exprimant: Angl. to tinger.
Ἐνλέχια, folertia, calliditas: Angl. trick, & tricke, id est, sophismata: Ἐντυγχάνει, incurrit, convenit, quadrat, aptum est, to be trigg. in eam sententiam non semel audivisse mihi videor.
Εἱλέω, verto, volvo, εἱλεῖς circumplicari & obvolvi: Anglicè, a wheele, rota: item to wtlde, circumagere.
Εἴλλω, prohibeo; εἵλω, frenum, vinculum; εἵλαρ, propugnaculum: Angl. to hold; ut cum dicunt, hold your hand, abstine manum: item a hold; arx, propugnaculum.
Ἐρέω, ἐρέω, ἐρείνω, interrogo, denuncio, quæro, to errand.
Ἐθέαι, proprie, ἐκ τῆς κοσμουμένας, ἢ ἐπιμελείας ἐξ ἔθους ἀξιώματος. Cæsaries, ex more culta & ornata: ut Hesychius & Etymologicum explicant. Unde ἐθί-ἐμφυής,

page.notes: Greek words and English glosses in the margin are difficult; Greek accents and some glosses are uncertain. Right margin contains pencil marks, not printed text. Page is a 17th-century Anglo-Saxon glossary; a few Greek readings are approximate and should be checked against the scan.
